narrative: The color wheel is revealed as a construction of the mind rather than a feature of light: the visual system invents purple and magenta to close the open-ended spectrum into a circle, performing this transformation in retinal tissue that is embryologically brain. The chapter traces color experience through four distinct levels — physics, pigment chemistry, cone sampling, and opponent-channel recombination — showing why painters and physicists disagree about primary colors, why yellow feels primary despite having no dedicated cone, and how both co-evolution and deep neural networks converge on the same two opponent axes in response to the statistical structure of a sun-lit world.
